summary: When an IPv6 packet is sent to a multicast address on Ethernet, the address is normally mapped to an Ethernet multicast address. This standards-track document clarifies that in some circumstances the packet may instead be sent to an Ethernet unicast address. It updates RFC 2464.

plainLanguage.summary: An IPv6 packet addressed to a multicast group can sometimes be sent to one Ethernet address when only one address is relevant. A receiver must accept the packet rather than dropping it for this reason.

subtitle: An IPv6 multicast packet may use an Ethernet unicast address when one address matters.

tldr.problem: The existing IPv6-over-Ethernet mapping described multicast destinations as Ethernet multicast addresses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC permits an IPv6 packet with a multicast destination to map to an Ethernet unicast address when only one address is relevant.
tldr.outcome: The new mapping extends, but does not replace, RFC 2464. A receiver must not drop such a packet because of the mapping.

facts.label: Receiver requirement
facts.value: MUST NOT drop the packet because of this mapping

today: RFC 6085 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2464. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6085.

sections.title: Extending the Ethernet Mapping
sections.content:
Section 7 of RFC 2464 describes mapping an IPv6 packet with a multicast destination address to an Ethernet link-layer address. RFC 6085 explicitly allows the mapping to use an Ethernet link-layer unicast address when it is clear that only one address is relevant.

This extension does not replace the mapping in RFC 2464. Determining the unicast Ethernet address and constructing the outgoing IPv6 packet are outside this document's scope.
sections.plainLanguage: A multicast destination does not always require an Ethernet multicast address. When only one Ethernet address is relevant, the packet may use that unicast address instead.

sections.title: Receiving a Multicast Packet
sections.content: An IPv6 node that receives a packet with a multicast destination address and an Ethernet link-layer unicast address MUST NOT drop the packet because this form of address mapping was used.
sections.plainLanguage: A receiving IPv6 node must not discard a multicast packet just because its Ethernet address is unicast.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that this document does not introduce any new security vulnerabilities. It gives no further security analysis.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC reports no new security vulnerabilities from this mapping clarification.

references.text: Crawford, M., "Transmission of IPv6 Packets over Ethernet Networks", RFC 2464, December 1998.
